features.note: Form unchanged; the interaction legend is placed BOTTOM-LEFT (away from the procedencia panel and the projected-bbox corner that produced the framing-probe false positive).

THE INTERACTION INSIGHT. The inherited pick() stopped at the first VISIBLE surface — correct for solids (a click can't pass through a solid body; abandoning it once made a sibling asset report a hotspot behind a housing as clickable). But it is FALSE FOR A VEIL: the whole point of this subject is seeing THROUGH the bubble (framing proves 43/43 of the front element is eye-reachable through it), and a user clicking the lens they can plainly see, only to be blocked by glass they are looking through, would rightly call it broken. New rule: the click passes through TRANSPARENT surfaces and stops at the first OPAQUE one — the SAME criterion the framing check uses for eye-visibility, so eye-reachability and click-reachability coincide. The bubble stays a hotspot at LOWER priority (responds only where nothing opaque is behind the ray: click glass over void -> dome lifts; click glass over lens -> get the lens). Negative control: making the bubble opaque breaks lens reachability (the click stops at dome_bubble) — without it the rule would be indistinguishable from 'the ray reaches the lens anyway'.
Lens is a hotspot (cycle tilt), reachable through the bubble; 'Módulo óptico' reads blue in the legend from both hero and under.
Ring is a hotspot (collar/ceiling prop); 'Anillo de montaje' reachable in all states. Wordmark reads upright in under.

mechanical.notes: 11/11 suites. Console clean. Hotspots: lens (cycle tilt), collar (ceiling prop), yoke (change view), dome (remove bubble). TWO defects, the second the more important: (1) overlapping hotspot subtrees — the yoke hotspot addressed pan_yoke, which is ALSO the cradle's parent, so it addressed a node CONTAINING the optics and every sampled point landed on the lens (reported unreachable, blocked by lens, from any angle); two hotspot subtrees that contain each other are ambiguous by construction, so the arms moved to their own yoke_arms group (declared in the spec hierarchy). (2) the check's OWN CRITERION was wrong: it required every hotspot reachable FROM THE HERO, but the yoke arms live inside the shroud cone (hidden from the oblique hero, plainly there down the cone mouth in the near-axial under view) — satisfying that would mean either pulling structural pieces out of the housing that holds them or declaring a working affordance broken, neither true. Correct criterion: reachable in SOME declared capture state, with the LEGEND DIMMING what is not reachable right now (what a static capture owes a viewer with no cursor). Verified in --page: hero dims 'Horquilla de soporte'; under lights it and dims 'Cúpula' — the legend re-derives per view and distinguishes something (not all rows lit regardless). State is actually driven (4 interactions each change tilt/ceiling/view/dome, read before/after); __qaInteract('nope') returns ok:false with an error, not silence; solids still block (a collar click stops at base_body); framing/optics 43-43/lighting/float all unchanged.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The pass's insight is genuinely novel and correct: for a see-through subject, click-reachability must match EYE-reachability, so the pick() ray passes through transparent surfaces and stops at the first opaque one — the same rule the framing check uses — with the bubble kept as a lower-priority hotspot and proven by a negative control (opaque bubble blocks the lens). The two defects (self-containing hotspot subtrees; a hero-only reachability criterion that would have condemned a working in-cone affordance) were both fixed at the criterion level, and the legend's per-view dimming (verified flipping between hero and under) is exactly what a static capture owes a cursor-less viewer. Cleared to the optimization pass.
